title: incident-bot: oncall runbook autodiagnostics suggestions + SLO toolkit integration
author: Evan Brooks
description: Motivation: Improve on-call efficacy by surfacing contextual runbook links and automated SLO diagnostic suggestions directly in incident-bot alerts. This PR adds a lightweight suggestion engine that correlates SLO violations from slo-toolkit with matching runbooks and pre-populated diagnostic steps. The feature is opt-in via a new incident-bot config flag (enable_autosuggestions) and integrates with the existing runbook index and SLO metadata service. Summary of changes: 1) runbook matcher service: fuzzy-matching and metadata scoring for SLO -> runbook linking; 2) suggestion templates: predefined templates for common diagnostics (k8s pod restarts, high queue latency, redis saturation) with auto-populated commands and dashboard links; 3) SLO toolkit adapter: pulls recent SLO evaluation context and top error signals to seed suggestions; 4) on-call helper UI: compact suggestion card with quick links for runbook, dashboards, and a one-click create-postmortem draft; 5) telemetry: new metrics (incidentbot.suggestions.shown, .accepted, .rejected) and tracing spans for matcher latency; 6) tests and docs: unit + integration tests and updated README/ops-runbooks doc. Backwards compatibility: feature disabled by default; no change to existing alert payloads when disabled. Rollout plan: staged rollout to internal teams -> beta customers, guardrail via metrics and canary ratio. See linked Linear tickets for acceptance criteria and dashboard queries. Testing: unit tests for matcher heuristics, end-to-end test that verifies suggestion card appears for synthetic SLO violation events, manual QA for various runbook link quality. Notes: kept matcher tunable via config thresholds to reduce false positives; suggestion templates are editable via ops-runbooks repo.
commits: feat(matcher): add runbook metadata scoring and fuzzy title matching
feat(adapter): integrate slo-toolkit context extractor (pulls recent error signatures)
feat(ui): add compact suggestion card and create-postmortem flow

docs: update incident-bot README and oncall runbooks guide
perf: cache runbook index in memory with TTL to reduce lookup latency
review_comments: Ava Martinez: Nice work. Two requests: 1) add a unit test for the title fuzzy match edge-case (abbreviations), and 2) ensure matcher uses existing cache util rather than ad-hoc TTL. Please also call out privacy implications for runbooks with customer-sensitive content.

Evan Brooks (author): Added test for abbreviations and moved caching to shared cache util. For sensitive runbooks we now respect runbook.metadata.visibility and skip suggestions; updated docs to mention this.
Noah Chen: Can we add a small e2e that simulates SLO toolkit payloads with multiple error-signatures? Concerned about noise if the top signal is low-volume errors.
Evan Brooks (author): Added an integration test that seeds 3 error signatures and asserts the top 2 are used; added threshold config to suppress low-volume signals.
Priya Singh: Telemetry looks good but add a failure counter when matcher fails to find a runbook so we can track coverage.
Evan Brooks (author): Added incidentbot.suggestions.miss_count metric and a Grafana panel to the suggestions dashboard.
Liam O'Connor: Docs look good. For rollout, recommend enabling for internal teams only with a 5% canary for external customers. Approving pending canary config.
Evan Brooks (author): Canary config added to deploy/config/incident-bot-defaults.yaml. Marking ready for merge.
merge_outcome: merged via squash (squash and merge). Commit message prefixed with feat(incident-bot): runbook autodiagnostics suggestions + slo-toolkit integration
release_notes: Added opt-in incident-bot feature that surfaces runbook and SLO diagnostic suggestions in alerts. Disabled by default. Includes telemetry and docs. Tweakable via incident-bot config.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature by setting deploy/config/incident-bot-defaults.yaml -> enable_autosuggestions: true for canary group. Monitor incidentbot.suggestions.* metrics and suggestions.dashboard. If false positives rise, increase matcher.min_score or reduce top_k_suggestions.
